questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the candidate's ability to compose namespace-scoped config reloads using standard primitives (InitContainers, sidecars, Secrets, PVCs, and NetworkPolicies) without custom operators, focusing on reliability and reload semantics.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer bootstraps config from central API
- Sidecar monitors config changes and signals main app
- Secrets for API tokens and credentials
- Shared volume for config sync
- PVC for logs and /logs
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricts egress to config API

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-reload
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: config
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: logs-claim
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: your-app:latest
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/app/config
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /var/log/app
        - name: reloader
          image: myorg/config-reloader:latest
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do sleep 300; done"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/app/config
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate config before applying a hot reload?
- How would you handle partial reload failures or rollback?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses CKAD fundamentals, including CronJobs, PVCs, ConfigMaps, InitContainers, Secrets, TLS sidecars, probes, and NetworkPolicies within a realistic risk-based scenario.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and backoff management
- PVC-mounted configuration discovery
- YAML validation with yq for key extraction
- InitContainers for tool installation and sidecar patterns
- Secrets management and TLS certificate rotation
- Namespace-level network policy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: config-scan
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "0 0 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: yq-installer
            image: busybox:1.36
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              wget -O /usr/local/bin/yq https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.35.1/yq_linux_amd64
              chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
          containers:
          - name: scanner
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              for cm in $(kubectl get configmap -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
                kubectl get configmap $cm -o yaml | yq e '.data | keys' - | grep -v '^---\|config.json' && echo "$cm"
              done | curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d @- http://config-scan-portal:8080/api/v1/scan
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: config-scan-secret
                  key: api-key
            volumeMounts:
            - name: configs
              mountPath: /configs
          - name: tls-sidecar
            image: nginx:alpine
            ports:
            - containerPort: 443
              name: https
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /ready
                port: 443
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 443
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tls-certs
              mountPath: /etc/nginx/certs
              readOnly: true
          volumes:
          - name: configs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: config-scan-pvc
          - name: tmp
            emptyDir: {}
          - name: tls-certs
            secret:
              secretName: config-scan-tls
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: config-scan-pvc
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadOnlyMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-scan-secret
  namespace: target-namespace
type: Opaque
stringData:
  api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: config-scan-network-policy
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      job-name: config-scan
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: config-scan-portal
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **PVC vs ConfigMap listing**: Using a PVC requires storage provisioning but allows scanning ConfigMap YAML files directly. Listing ConfigMaps via kubectl is simpler but lacks filesystem semantics.
- **InitContainer vs sidecar image**: InitContainer adds startup latency but ensures a minimal base scanner image. A custom image with yq pre-installed reduces complexity but increases maintenance.
- **NetworkPolicy granularity**: Restricting egress improves security but may break if the target service endpoint changes. Consider DNS-based policies for flexibility.
- **Probes on sidecar**: Adding probes assumes the sidecar exposes health endpoints; this adds configuration overhead but enables reliable deployment in production clusters.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical RBAC scoping, in-cluster API access, and safe, repeatable audits in a real CKAD setup.

- CronJob per-namespace execution
- ServiceAccount with minimal RBAC
- In-cluster API access and report formatting
- InitContainer, Secrets, TLS rotation, probes

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal skeleton CronJob outline (not a full manifest)
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: namespace-audit
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: auditor-sa
```

- CronJob scheduling and pod template
- InitContainer for tool bootstrap

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob

  name: config-validator

  schedule: "*/3 * * * *"

      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: config-validator-sa
```

## Why This Is Asked
Practical CKAD tasks using ConfigMaps, env injection, probes, resources, and Service exposure. Demonstrates understanding of update strategies.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap usage via env/ENV
- Probes: readiness and liveness
- Resource requests/limits
- Service exposure and port mapping
- Rolling updates and rollout verification

## Code Example

```javascript
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: api-config
data:
  PORT: 3000
  APP_MODE: prod

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
template:
  metadata:
    labels:
      app: api
  spec:
    containers:
    - name: api
      image: my-api:1.0
      ports:
      - containerPort: 3000
      env:
      - name: PORT
        valueFrom:
          configMapKeyRef:
            name: api-config
            key: PORT
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 3000
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 3000
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 100m
          memory: 128Mi
        limits:
          cpu: 200m
          memory: 256Mi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: api
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you reload config without pod restart?
- How do you verify a rolling update complete with zero downtime?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a one-off reconciliation Job that interacts with external services, ensures idempotent processing via a fingerprint, and properly configures InitContainers, Secrets, and backoff behavior. It also checks handling of PVC-mounted data and rollback planning.


## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes Job with backoff and deadline
- InitContainer for bootstrap tooling
- PVC mounting and data access in a one-off task
- yq for YAML extraction
- Idempotent design via server fingerprint key
- Secret and ConfigMap usage for credentials and endpoints
- Rollback and observability considerations


## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: data-ingest-audit-reconcile
spec:
  backoffLimit: 4
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 900
  template:
    metadata:
      name: data-ingest-audit-reconcile
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: reconciler
        image: your-registry/audit-client:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "set -e; /bin/reconcile.sh /data/manifests.yaml"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /data
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq && curl -L -o /usr/local/bin/yq https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.9.6/yq_linux_amd64 && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /data
      restartPolicy: Never
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-manifests
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: regcred
```


## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test idempotency in CI/CD?
- How would you scale this for larger manifest sets without timeouts?
- How would you monitor and rollback on failure?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD workflow patterns: CronJobs, batch processing, and secret management within a namespace; validates knowledge of init containers, sidecars, and network hardening.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling in a namespace
- InitContainer dependency installation
- ConfigMap for BATCH_SIZE
- Secret for API credentials
- Sidecar for TLS cert rotation
- NetworkPolicy for internal egress controls
- Probes for readiness and liveness
- Idempotency vs at-least-once semantics

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: csv-ingest
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: install-csvkit
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'pip install csvkit && cp -r /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/* /shared/']
            volumeMounts:
            - name: shared-libs
              mountPath: /shared
          containers:
          - name: csv-processor
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'python /app/process.py']
            env:
            - name: BATCH_SIZE
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: app-config
                  key: BATCH_SIZE
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-credentials
                  key: token
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data-pvc
              mountPath: /data
            - name: shared-libs
              mountPath: /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 30
          - name: cert-rotator
            image: cert-manager/cert-manager-rotator
            volumeMounts:
            - name: certs
              mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs
          volumes:
          - name: data-pvc
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: data-pvc
          - name: shared-libs
            emptyDir: {}
          - name: certs
            emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-config
data:
  BATCH_SIZE: "10"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-credentials
type: Opaque
data:
  token: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: csv-ingest-netpol
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: csv-ingest
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: data-portal
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **CronJob vs Deployment**: CronJobs provide scheduled execution but lack continuous availability; Deployments offer always-on processing but require custom scheduling logic.
- **InitContainer overhead**: Installing dependencies at runtime increases startup time vs pre-built images, but provides flexibility for version updates.
- **Sidecar complexity**: TLS cert rotation adds operational overhead but ensures security compliance; alternative is using cert-manager injection.
- **Batch processing**: Larger batches improve throughput but increase memory usage and failure impact; smaller batches provide better isolation but higher API call frequency.
- **NetworkPolicy scope**: Namespace-scoped policies provide good isolation but require per-namespace management; cluster-wide policies simplify administration but reduce granular control.
- **Storage patterns**: PVC-backed storage ensures data persistence across pod restarts but requires careful volume management; temporary storage simplifies cleanup but risks data loss during failures.

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design per-namespace automation with auditability and tight network controls. Image provenance is a critical security concern for multi-tenant environments like Discord or Airbnb, where ensuring container images come from trusted registries is essential.

## Key Concepts
- **CKAD Scheduling**: CronJob for recurring audit tasks
- **Image Provenance**: Registry API integration, image digests (SHA256)
- **Secrets & ConfigMaps**: REGISTRY_TOKEN for authentication, audit-status for state tracking
- **PV-backed Storage**: PVC at /audit for persistent digest reports
- **InitContainers**: Installing required tools (curl, jq) for image inspection
- **Readiness Probes**: Ensuring the pod is ready before accepting traffic
- **Namespace NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress to only trusted registries

```yaml
          initContainers:
          - name: tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
          containers:
          - name: auditor
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "..."]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
            - name: registry-token
              mountPath: /secrets
              readOnly: true
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["sh", "-c", "[ -f /audit/ready ]"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
          volumes:
          - name: audit-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: audit-pvc
          - name: registry-token
            secret:
              secretName: REGISTRY_TOKEN
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-status
  namespace: target-namespace
data:
  last_run: ""
  digest_count: "0"
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: registry-egress
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: registry
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **CronJob vs Job**: CronJob provides scheduling but has slight timing drift; use precise timing if required.
- **PVC Size**: Allocate sufficient storage based on pod count and audit frequency.
- **InitContainer Overhead**: Adds startup time but ensures tools are available; consider using a custom image with pre-installed tools.
- **NetworkPolicy Scope**: A permissive egress may be necessary if multiple registries are used; balance security with operational flexibility.
- **ConfigMap Updates**: Frequent updates may cause contention; consider annotation-based status or external database for high-frequency audits.

questions.explanation:
This question assesses CKAD-level ability to compose a batch job with initialization steps, configuration management, and access controls. It also evaluates understanding of idempotence and rollback planning.

**Key Concepts**
- CronJob scheduling and `concurrencyPolicy` for preventing concurrent runs
- InitContainer for dependency installation
- ConfigMap and Secret mounting patterns
- PVC usage across Job pods
- Readiness and Liveness probes for batch workloads
- NetworkPolicy for egress restrictions

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-migrate
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  backoffLimit: 3
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: busybox
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'wget -O /usr/local/bin/yq ... && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq']
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          containers:
          - name: migrate
            image: curlimages/curl
            args: ['sh', '-c', 'yq -o=json /manifests/*.yaml > /out/manifests.json']
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ['test', '-f', '/out/manifests.json']
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
              periodSeconds: 30
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ['sh', '-c', 'ls /out']
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 60
            volumeMounts:
            - name: manifests
              mountPath: /manifests
            - name: out
              mountPath: /out
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: credentials
          volumes:
          - name: manifests
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: manifest-pvc
          - name: out
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: manifest-pvc
          - name: config
            configMap:
              name: migrate-options
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

**Rollback Strategy**: To rollback, either suspend the CronJob with `kubectl patch cronjob data-migrate -n analytics -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'` or reduce the `successfulJobsHistoryLimit` to 0 to prevent new Jobs from being created.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates practical Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) skills across multiple resource types and patterns in a realistic production scenario. It tests the ability to compose distributed system components while understanding security boundaries.

## Key Concepts Tested

1. **ConfigMap/Secret Integration**: Properly referencing ConfigMap values and Secret data as environment variables to configure the application.

2. **InitContainer Pattern**: Performing one-time setup tasks—like installing tools—before the main application container starts.

3. **Sidecar Containers**: Running auxiliary containers alongside the main application for cross-cutting concerns like TLS certificate management.

4. **Health Probes**: Configuring readiness and liveness probes to manage pod traffic and restart behavior.

5. **NetworkPolicy**: Restricting network egress to enforce least-privilege access between namespaces and services.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

- Forgetting to mount ConfigMap/Secret values into the container environment
- Not handling signal propagation in infinite loops (leading to graceful shutdown issues)
- Overly restrictive NetworkPolicies that block necessary egress routes
- Misconfiguring probe thresholds that cause premature restarts or delayed traffic routing

## Why This Is Asked
Tests CronJob usage, PVs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, probes, and NetworkPolicy in a realistic backup workflow.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling from ConfigMap
- PVC mounts and tar packaging
- InitContainer tooling prep
- Secret-based credentials for remote backups
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy egress controls

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-backup
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: installer
              image: busybox
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - apk add --no-cache tar pigz
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: alpine:3.18
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - tar -czf /backup/namespace-$(date +%F-%H%M).tar.gz -C /data .
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: backup
                  mountPath: /backup
              readinessProbe:
                exec:
                  command:
                    - cat
                    - /tmp/healthy
                initialDelaySeconds: 30
                periodSeconds: 60
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /healthz
                  port: 8080
          volumes:
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: backup
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to extend to remote storage? 
- How to implement retention and idempotent backups?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: PVCs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, sidecars, readiness/liveness, and network policies in a realistic static content scenario.

Key Concepts
- PVC-backed volumes and ConfigMap mounts
- InitContainer for initial bootstrap
- Sidecar for live file reloads
- ConfigMap-driven content flags
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-content-server
  namespace: ckad-demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: static-content
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: static-content
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: html
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: static-content-pvc
        - name: template
          configMap:
            name: page-template
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: page-config
      initContainers:
        - name: init
          image: alpine
          command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /template/index.html /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
            - name: template
              mountPath: /template
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:alpine
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
        - name: reload-agent
          image: busybox
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do inotifywait -e modify /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html; nginx -s reload; done"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /index.html
          port: 80
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /index.html
          port: 80
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
```

Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle multi-namespace isolation if the same config is needed across namespaces?
- What changes if you switch to an A/B testing banner using two ConfigMaps and a canary rollout?
